speaker: legionary
personality: Tired veteran of the old Third Cohort; resents taking orders from the Federation, respects plain talk and local pride.

openings.text: Hold it there. The radio's been going on about a stranger all night, and you look like a stranger.
You. Papers. And don't tell me you're Federation, I can smell a local from here.

exchanges.prompt: Twenty-two years in the Third Cohort, and now I check papers for the Federation. So what are you doing on my street after curfew?

replies.text: Going home. My mother's off Via dei Tribunali, and they moved the curfew again.
replies.reaction: They move it every week. Keeps us guessing.

replies.text: The Federation keeps these streets safe. You should be proud to serve it.
replies.reaction: Proud. Is that what they told you to say?

replies.text: Same as you. Doing what the Federation tells me and hating every minute of it.
replies.reaction: Ha. At least you're honest about it.

replies.text: Lantern, six-two. Detached duty. Run it through your relay if you like.
replies.reaction: That's this week's code. You could have led with it.

exchanges.prompt: The Third used to mean something. Now we stand at barriers while their trucks drive through without stopping. Know what's in those trucks?

replies.text: No. But I know the old Third would never have waved them through without a look.
replies.reaction: We wouldn't have. My centurion would have opened every one.

replies.text: Supplies, I'd guess. Not my business.
replies.reaction: That's what everyone says. Not my business.

replies.text: No idea. But here's {cost} for a man who doesn't ask either.
replies.reaction: I'll take it. Doesn't mean I like you.

replies.text: If the Third had fought harder, the Federation wouldn't be here.
replies.reaction: Say that again. Go on, say it again.

exchanges.prompt: Last question, so think first. If I let you walk and you're trouble, it's my neck. Why should I care about yours?

replies.text: Because I'll report you if you don't.
replies.reaction: Report me to who? The Federation would thank me for locking you up.

replies.text: You don't have to. But you didn't serve twenty-two years to arrest Neapolitans for them.
replies.reaction: No. I didn't.

replies.text: Because I'll be gone before your shift ends, and nobody will know you stopped me.
replies.reaction: That's not a reason. But it helps.

closings.success: Go on, then. I never saw you, and you never saw me.
closings.failure: That's enough. Hands on your head. Checkpoint four, I've got one here!

speaker: legionary
personality: Nervous recruit three weeks into the job; terrified of his Federation sergeant, calmed by reassurance and anything that sounds like proper procedure.

openings.text: Stop! Stop there. They said on the radio to stop everyone. Please don't move.
Halt. Um, citizen, halt. Identity card, please. I have to check everyone. It's the rules.

exchanges.prompt: It's my third week. If the sergeant sees me let someone through without a card, I'm finished. Where's your card?

replies.text: Left it at work. I know. Write me up for it, I'll pay the fine.
replies.reaction: A fine, yes. There's a form for that, I think.

replies.text: You're doing it right. Breathe. Nobody's watching, and I'm not going to make trouble for you.
replies.reaction: Okay. Thank you, nobody ever says that to me.

replies.text: Third week? Run home to your mother, boy.
replies.reaction: I don't have to take that. I could call this in.

replies.text: Lantern, six-two. Detached duty. Your sergeant will tell you that means no search.
replies.reaction: Lantern six-two, that's on the card they gave us. Sorry, I didn't know.

exchanges.prompt: They told us anyone out after curfew could be a saboteur. You don't look like one. What do saboteurs look like?

replies.text: I couldn't tell you.
replies.reaction: Nobody can. That's what scares me.

replies.text: Exactly like me. You'd better shoot me now.
replies.reaction: Don't say that! Don't joke about that, please.

replies.text: I'd guess they don't stop when a legionary tells them to.
replies.reaction: That's true. You did stop.

replies.text: Like people who run. I'm standing here answering your questions. Put that in your log.
replies.reaction: Standing still, answering questions. Yes, I can write that.

exchanges.prompt: My mother says the Federation are taking people. My sergeant says that's rebel talk. If I let you go and you're a rebel, they'll take me instead.

replies.text: Nobody's taking you. Log me as a cleared civilian, curfew warning given. That's all this is.
replies.reaction: Cleared civilian, curfew warning. That's a real category, that's fine.

replies.text: Your mother's right. Desert while you still can.
replies.reaction: Desert? Are you trying to get me shot?

replies.text: Then here's {cost}. Give it to your mother, and forget my face.
replies.reaction: I really shouldn't. She does need it, though.

replies.text: If I were a rebel, would I be standing here chatting with a legionary?
replies.reaction: No. I suppose you wouldn't.

closings.success: Go. Quickly, before somebody sees. And be careful out there.
closings.failure: No. No, I'm calling it in. I'm sorry. Control, this is post nine, I have a suspect!

speaker: legionary
personality: Bored, quietly corrupt legionary who treats the occupation as a racket; wants gossip, a deal or cash, and has no patience for speeches.

openings.text: Everyone's jumpy tonight. Sirens, radios, Federation officers shouting at us. And now you. Make it interesting.
Evening. Checkpoint's closed. Well, closed to most people. Depends how the conversation goes.

exchanges.prompt: Eight hours on this corner. Nothing to read, nothing to smoke, nobody worth talking to. Tell me something I don't know.

replies.text: Curfew's moving up again next month. Earlier every time.
replies.reaction: Old news. But fine, points for trying.

replies.text: This isn't the time for gossip. People are disappearing.
replies.reaction: People are always disappearing. Doesn't make my shift any shorter.

replies.text: Lantern, six-two. Detached duty. Want to explain to my lieutenant why you held me up?
replies.reaction: Lantern six-two, look at you with the proper words. Fine, fine.

replies.text: The prefect's aide leaves the Federation officers' club at dawn. Twice this week, same coat.
replies.reaction: Has he now. That's worth something in the barracks.

exchanges.prompt: You know what this job pays? The Empire paid in denarii. The Federation pays in vouchers for their own canteens. So what's in it for me?

replies.text: I'll tell your centurion you're shaking people down at checkpoints.
replies.reaction: My centurion takes a cut. Try again.

replies.text: Nothing. So why work hard for them? Wave me through and save yourself the paperwork.
replies.reaction: Now there's a philosophy I can respect.

replies.text: {cost}. Real money, not vouchers.
replies.reaction: Now you're speaking my language.

replies.text: The satisfaction of a job well done.
replies.reaction: Is that what they're calling it now.

exchanges.prompt: Here's the thing. The Federation pays a bonus for every curfew-breaker brought in. Why shouldn't I collect it on you?

replies.text: Because I'm worth more to you outside a cell. I hear things, and I come through here often.
replies.reaction: A regular. I like regulars.

replies.text: Because these are our streets, not theirs. Remember whose side you're on.
replies.reaction: My side's the one that pays. I've heard that speech before.

replies.text: Because the bonus is paid in vouchers, and it takes three forms to claim.
replies.reaction: Four forms, actually. You're not wrong.

closings.success: Off you go, then. Pleasure doing business.
closings.failure: No sale. Hey! Over here! I've got a curfew-breaker for the bonus!
